checks.check: Retired temporary handles stay memory-only and reserve one existing session resource slot until close completes across roots. [[c1]]
checks.evidence: TemporaryDriverResources.commitRemoval (session-resources.ts:101-111) calls the injected retainRemovalSlot() exactly once per committed removal and only releases it inside RemovalRetirementOwner.commit's close callback after retire() resolves (session-resources.ts:109-110). session-entries.ts:56-60 wires retainRemovalSlot to increment/decrement the SAME session budget counter (#budget.retired) used by #quota (session-entries.ts:68), so a retirement consumes an existing MAX_SESSION_CONNECTIONS slot rather than a fresh one. The cross-root sharing is exercised directly in session-resources.test.ts:50-70 ('CM-S4-TEMP: retired resources retain a shared slot across roots...'): two TemporaryDriverResources instances for rootA/rootB share one `retain` callback; shared.slots stays 1 from commitRemoval until the retried close succeeds, and only drops to 0 after that close completes, with sibling root B's own resource (otherCloses) left untouched. Driver construction still goes through fileExecutionPolicy(...,{persistence:'memory-only'}) (session-resources.ts:44), consistent with 'memory-only'.

checks.check: Failed closes retain exact handles; session end/expiry/shutdown cancel/drain owned resources without fresh admission or arbitrary source cleanup. [[c1]]
checks.evidence: retire()/#closeFile() mark only the failing record/file and keep it in #records / fileClosures until a successful retry (session-resources.ts:63-128); the 'removal' flag suppresses the #failedClose session-wide circuit-breaker only for committed removals so other owners aren't poisoned (session-resources.ts:69,106,124). session-resources.test.ts:50-70 and :72-86 show a failing close is retried and only the exact handle (calls===1 throws, retry succeeds) is affected, with no effect on a sibling resource. session-cleanup.test.ts:23-38 ('shutdown drains retained resources at capacity...') fills 64 revisions, calls close() (shutdown), observes it reject 'recovery-required' while slots stay at 1 (the failed one), asserts prepareRemoval now throws 'session-expired' (no fresh admission after stopAdmission), then clears the failure and re-closes to drain the last retained slot. session-cleanup.test.ts:40-54 ('cancellation and owner expiry...') exercises prepareRemoval/cancelRemoval/commitRemoval ordering plus a late-constructing driver that is still closed exactly once when owner close()+construction race, with slots returning to 0.

verdict.reason: Both acceptance checks are genuinely met by the code in session-resources.ts/session-entries.ts and are exercised by all 4 named CM-S4-TEMP test cases, which the daemon reports as passing; scope stayed inside session-resources.ts and the existing session-entries.ts budget port, matching the stated surface and leaving t6/t7's surfaces (secrets.ts, management.ts) untouched. However the daemon's own Tests check is FAILED: the same run of session-cleanup.test.ts shows two pre-existing CM-S3-EXPIRY/CM-S3-RECONNECT tests failing on a spawned-child reporter-format mismatch ('# pass 24' expected vs the child's actual 'ℹ pass 24' output) unrelated to this Task's code, but a failing check result fails the Task regardless of my judgment of the two acceptance checks.
